criteria.statement: When the merge step runs in the reproduction scenario, it brings the local branch up to the moved head B before the custody gate, and the gate (`custody.js reconcile ... --head B`) then does not refuse — the step does not return `stop` with "local HEAD has shipped changes not on the PR head (or the PR head has changes not pulled here): src/c.js"
criteria.cites: §Reproduction Steps 1–3; Actual (the refusal JSON and "Nothing in the run changes the local branch … Root cause [ran]"); Expected ¶1 "brings the local branch to the branch head … passes the custody gate"
criteria.evidence: Transcript of the reproduction replayed in a scratch repo with a bare origin (or on github-live-test): `git rev-parse HEAD` printing B after the merge step's catch-up, followed by the gate's `custody.js reconcile` JSON for `--head B` with an action other than `refused`

criteria.statement: The merge step waits for CI on the moved head B even though B was pushed by another session rather than by the merge step's own merge-in, and does not reach `gh pr merge` before a CI result for B has been seen
criteria.cites: §Reproduction Actual ¶2 "`ship-primitive-merge.md` step 1 waits for CI only on 'a head this step pushed by merge-in' … Fixing only the refusal would let the merge go ahead on B with no CI result seen for B"; Expected ¶1 "waits for CI on it"; Expected ¶2 (issue #98) "repeat the `push` and `wait-ci` steps … against the new head"
criteria.evidence: Ship-run transcript on github-live-test (or the ship-build seam test driving the sequencer) showing a CI wait (`gh pr checks <pr>` / the wait-ci result) naming head B, ordered before the `gh pr merge` call

criteria.statement: When CI fails on the moved head B, the merge step does not merge B: it returns `red` naming B as the head, so the run enters the existing red-head fix loop instead of merging or ending STUCK
criteria.cites: §Reproduction Actual ¶2 "Fixing only the refusal would let the merge go ahead on B with no CI result seen for B" (waiting on B exists to keep a red B from merging); domain-derived: a CI wait whose failing result still let the merge proceed would prove nothing, so a failing result on B must block the merge
criteria.evidence: Ship-run transcript or seam-test output for a moved head whose CI is failing: the merge step's result `red` with `data.head` equal to B and the failing check names, and no `gh pr merge` call for B

criteria.statement: When the moved head B has passed CI and the custody gate, the merge step merges it pinned to B: `gh pr merge <pr> --<method> --match-head-commit B` (the new head, not the earlier head A)
criteria.cites: §Reproduction Expected ¶1 "merges it with `--match-head-commit <new head>`"; Expected ¶2 (issue #98) "It should then merge that head"; Actual ¶3 (the Storybook banners naming `--match-head-commit A`)
criteria.evidence: Ship-run transcript on github-live-test showing the `gh pr merge … --match-head-commit <B>` command, and the PR's merge record showing B as the merged head

criteria.statement: On the moved head B the merge step collects review findings when B's change over the last judged head is more than a base merge, and does not require a findings round when the change is only a base merge
criteria.cites: §Reproduction Expected ¶1 "collects findings on it when it is more than a base merge"; Expected ¶2 (issue #98) "(and `collect-findings` when the diff is not base-only)"
criteria.evidence: Two ship-run transcripts (or seam-test cases): one where B adds a non-base commit, showing a `collect-findings` result recorded against B; one where B is a base merge only, showing the step going on to the custody gate with no `collect-findings` round

criteria.statement: Each step that judges a head records which head it judged (`wait-ci` and `collect-findings` record the head they ruled on), and a head that `request-review` or `await-approval` merely observed is not treated as judged — so the merge step can tell that B is not the head the run last judged
criteria.cites: §Reproduction Actual ¶2 "no step records WHICH head it judged: `wait-ci` and `collect-findings` record no head, while `request-review` and `await-approval` record the PR's head without judging it, so `context.head` cannot tell a judged head from an observed one"; Expected ¶1 "whenever the merge step finds the branch head is not the head the run last judged"
criteria.evidence: The run record (`shipped.json` step entries, or the sequencer's context in a seam test) showing a judged-head value on the `wait-ci` / `collect-findings` entries equal to A, and the merge step treating B as unjudged even after a `request-review` or `await-approval` entry recorded B

criteria.statement: Bringing the local branch up to the moved head never discards shipped work: if the local branch holds shipped commits that are not on the PR head, the catch-up does not overwrite them, and the custody gate still refuses that genuine divergence rather than merging
criteria.cites: domain-derived: the refusal reason quoted in §Reproduction Actual ("local HEAD has shipped changes not on the PR head") is custody's guard against merging something other than what was verified; a catch-up that reset the branch to B would silence the guard by deleting the very changes it protects, so the fix must cure only the case where B is ahead of local
criteria.evidence: Scratch-repo transcript: a local commit touching a shipped file that was never pushed, plus a moved PR head B; the merge step's output showing that local commit still present (`git log` naming it) and a gate result of `refused` (or a `stop`) with no `gh pr merge`
